claim_card.objects: Stationary spherical component with ordinary measurable nonnegative isotropic distribution f(E), E=psi-v^2/2, f(E)=0 for E<=0; continuous finite relative potential near a finite outer boundary, psi>0 inside and psi->0 at boundary; density finite at some interior psi0>0.
claim_card.conclusion: rho(psi)=o(sqrt(psi)) and therefore rho->0. A finite positive one-sided density at a jump to vacuum is incompatible. Literal X38/SC1 truncated cluster Burkert profiles have that jump and cannot realize this specified equilibrium.
claim_card.coefficient_domain: Real nonnegative functions and Lebesgue integrals; ordinary function f, not a distribution; finite positive Sigma,r0,rt in application.
no_additional_hypotheses_used: No numerical fit or finite scan
excluded_from_conclusion: Collisional fluids with different stress/boundary equations

dependency_graph.result: sqrt(psi0-E)>=sqrt(psi0/2) on [0,psi0/2] implies f integrable there.
No realization under stated isotropic no-wall hypotheses.

obligation_matrix.arbitrary_taper_sufficiency: not asserted; global DF remains open

small_case_and_boundary_checks: Constant positive f gives rho=(8pi sqrt2/3)f psi^(3/2), consistent with limit.
Integrable f~E^p for -1<p<0 still gives positive exponent p+3/2>1/2. Nonintegrable f near0 yields infinite density at every positive psi, not a finite jump.
At g_t=0, radial power translation may fail but continuity psi->0 leaves theorem intact.
B prime(x)=4x^2/[(1+x)(1+x^2)] yields the stated positive density; M continuous at rt means no surface mass delta.
strongest_safe_statement: Literal hard-truncated cluster profiles have no ordinary nonnegative isotropic stationary no-wall collisionless realization. Their empirical shear use can remain a declared boundary convention; this does not establish or exclude other dynamical profiles.
remaining_obligation: For any replacement, declare potential/DF/boundary and verify global positivity and Poisson consistency, then repeat common-profile observational fit. Anisotropic alternatives require separate analysis.
